hero.title: Backend & Distributed Systems Engineer
hero.status: Available for full-time roles from May 2027
hero.lede: I’m Ansh, a backend and distributed-systems engineer with 3.5 years in production. Most recently I was on Intuit’s Identity & Session Platform; before that I spent three and a half years at Headout, from intern to senior engineer. I’m finishing an MS in Computer Science at Stony Brook.
facts: MS Computer Science, Stony Brook · GPA 4.0
Stony Brook, NY · open to relocation
hero.sub: 3.5 years in production at Headout and Intuit. MS Computer Science at Stony Brook, GPA 4.0.

metrics.label: 503s per rollout
metrics.conditions: Per rolling deploy, Kubernetes preStop hooks

experience.title: Identity & Session Platform
experience.intro: Services powering SSO across TurboTax, QuickBooks, Credit Karma, and Mailchimp, spanning billions of token-validation requests for 100M+ customers at 99.9%+ availability.
bullets: Reduced p99 latency from **4.2s to 300ms** for bulk authorization in Intuit Enterprise Suite, scaling to **5,000 accounts/user at 200 TPS** via a rate-limited async batched-write path that removed DynamoDB hot-partition throttling.
Eliminated deployment-related 503 errors (**60+ to 0** per rollout) by adding graceful shutdown via Kubernetes preStop hooks.

experience.title: Creators Platform & Offers Management
experience.intro: Led backend for two new product surfaces at the top of Headout’s supply funnel.
bullets: Architected the **Creators Platform** backend from scratch as sole engineer (Spring Boot, Kafka, Redis), cutting onboarding from **13 days to 10 minutes** and growing collaborations from **50 to 700 creators per quarter**.
Reduced creator impression cost **80%** and raised 15-day content completion to **50%** by owning the event-driven content pipeline and economics.
Built **Offers Management** for supply partners with configurable discount controls: conversion up to **+30%**, **66%** adoption within a month, discount-related support tickets **-12%**.

experience.summary: Headout · Magic Listing, Novu, Hub migration
experience.title: Magic Listing · Novu · Hub
experience.intro: Backend infra that cut operational cost and unlocked scale.
bullets: **Magic Listing**: an AI-driven 3-step workflow replacing 60+ manual fields. Listing time **72 → 4 min** (-95%).
**Novu-based notifications**: schedule-request turnaround **-40%**, communication errors **-60%**.
**Schedule Management & Moderation**: one-click supplier-to-Hub migration. Processing time **-33%**, manual effort **-25%**.

experience.summary: Headout · Spring WebFlux · B2B Hub foundations
experience.title: Hub Backend Foundations
experience.intro: An early backend engineer on Hub, Headout’s B2B platform on Spring Boot WebFlux with REST & GraphQL APIs.
bullets: Enforced TDD for **96% code / 87% branch** coverage.
Re-architected the **London Theatre Direct** integration plugin as its owner. Order success rate **+80%**.
Spearheaded **Native Listing** for direct supply-partner integration. Operational efficiency **+30%**.

highlights: Teaching Assistant, SBU · CSE 416 & ISE/POL 369 · Spring 2026

projects.title: Column-Delta MVCC
projects.desc: Schema-aware MVCC in Mako. 69% less storage on TPC-C.
projects.intro: A schema-aware MVCC optimization in Mako that stores only modified columns.
bullets: **481 lines** of reusable C++ integrated into a distributed KV store.
**69%** MVCC storage reduction on TPC-C.
Within **1%** of baseline throughput.

reel.text: MVCC stores a new version of the whole row.
reel.sub: Column-Delta stores only the columns that changed.

reel.text: 481 lines of reusable C++ in Mako.

projects.title: VLFit
projects.desc: Fit-in spatial reasoning benchmark for 6 VLMs.
projects.intro: A vision-language benchmark for fit-in spatial reasoning with 220 image–question pairs across 60–70 categories.
bullets: Evaluated **6** state-of-the-art vision-language models.
The best reached only **60.9%**; numeric reasoning fell to **5.7%–22.9%**.

reel.text: Can a vision-language model tell if it fits?

reel.label: the best score among 6 state-of-the-art VLMs

projects.title: fxlang
projects.desc: An object-oriented language, from scratch in Rust.
projects.intro: An interpreted object-oriented language built from scratch in 2,300 lines of Rust.
bullets: Full pipeline: lexing, parsing, static resolution, and a **tree-walking interpreter**.
Classes, inheritance, closures, and lexical scoping.

reel.label: lines of Rust, from lexer to interpreter

projects.title: SAM
projects.desc: Face-recognition attendance. Smart India Hackathon winner.
projects.intro: A face-recognition attendance app for classrooms: offline-first mobile, a retrainable recognition pipeline, and weekly analytics.
bullets: **Smart India Hackathon 2022, Winner.** A national-level hackathon organized by the Government of India.
On-device retraining with TensorFlow Lite: new faces added in **under 8 seconds** on mid-range Android.
Analytics with weekly trends, anomaly flagging, and a light-touch appeal flow.

reel.sub: Offline-first, with a retrainable recognition pipeline.

reel.label: to add a new face, on-device
